title: Equal-volume foam costs of all enumerated TCP structures, and the N56 foam
description:
Minimal film area of equal-volume periodic foams (the Kelvin problem) for every tetrahedrally close-packed (TCP) structure enumerated by Dutour Sikirić, Delgado-Friedrichs and Deza (2010) and Dutour Sikirić and Deza (2012), plus nine alloy structures: 125 distinct topologies, relaxed with fixed topology and extrapolated to the continuum limit.

Weaire–Phelan (A15) remains the lowest (cost 5.28834). The enumerated structure N56 (I41/amd, 76 cells per unit cell) is second at 5.29400, 0.00019 (0.0036 %) below the σ phase (5.29419), confirmed independently with Surface Evolver 2.70. Only 10 of the 125 topologies beat Kelvin's foam.

Contents: catalogue (CSV), structure data (JSON, source .cgd files), Python relaxation and verification code, archived results, Surface Evolver input and output files, and a report. Code is MIT-licensed; data, results, figures and text are CC BY 4.0. Structure topologies are adapted from M. Dutour Sikirić, Dataset and programs for the work on space-fullerenes (Zenodo record 13691342, CC BY 4.0). Code and computations were produced with the help of an AI assistant (Anthropic's Claude) under the direction of the author, who is responsible for the content. Corrections and challenges: https://github.com/HyukdongKim/tcp-foam-catalog/issues
